tags.name: npl-agent
tags.summary: Describes one AI agent: its name, type, and how it should behave.
tags.description: You write the agent's name, type, and rules as attributes and text. The page shows them as a tidy card. Machines can read the same fields back.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: required. The agent's identifier, the `⌜<agent-name>` field of the source form. Mirrored to `data-name` after upgrade (the resolved value — an authored `data-name` is never overwritten).

attributes.name: type
attributes.description: required. The agent's archetype (e.g. `scout`, `coder`). Mirrored to `data-type` after upgrade (the resolved value).

attributes.name: version
attributes.description: required. The NPL contract version, the `NPL@{version}` field of the source form. Mirrored to `data-version` after upgrade (the resolved value).

attributes.name: extends
attributes.description: optional. The parent agent this definition extends; the header omits it when not authored. Mirrored to `data-extends` after upgrade (the resolved value).

tags.name: npl-artifact
tags.summary: Shows a piece of work an agent produced, like code or a report, with a title and notes.
tags.description: Wrap the artifact's title and content in this element and the page adds a frame around them. The content itself is never changed.

attributes.name: type
attributes.description: (unset). A content type such as `text`, `code`, `svg`, `markdown`. `svg` routes the content through a sandboxed iframe; every other value (including unset) renders the content preformatted. Mirrored to `data-type` (dual-form contract; the mirror is deferred past parse via afterParse).

tags.name: npl-cot
tags.summary: Shows the steps of a chain of thought, folded up until the reader opens them.
tags.description: Each step is listed in order, with the final answer at the end. The list uses a plain details box, so it works even with JavaScript off.

attributes.name: collapsed
attributes.description: Absent ⇒ the block starts expanded; present ⇒ it starts collapsed. Sets the **initial** open state of the native details; the user's own toggling is never re-forced. The runtime mirrors the boolean to `data-collapsed` (`"true"`/`"false"`) in `updated()` via afterParse — a write for CSS/extraction parity, never an input (the component reads the bare attribute only, like the sem tier's `collapsed`); the mirror is deferred past parse so a sem-source snapshot never sees runtime writes.

tags.name: npl-critique
tags.summary: Shows a review of one thing from one point of view: strengths, weaknesses, and a verdict.
tags.description: You write the subject, the strengths, the weaknesses, and the verdict. The element lays them out as a clean, labelled review card.

attributes.name: id
attributes.description: per the global attribute catalog — optional, the native HTML `id`; the only attribute parameter. No component-specific parameters exist; all content rides the five authored children.

tags.name: npl-declaration
tags.summary: Shows which version of a rules document you are reading.
tags.description: It renders the version line of an NPL document, such as NPL@1.0, as a banner at the top. Extended documents are marked the same way.

attributes.name: version
attributes.description: required; a missing version warns and the banner still renders, with the bare mark (`⌜NPL@⌝`). Rendered in the banner mark (`⌜NPL@<version>⌝`) and mirrored to `data-version` (dual-form contract; the mirror is deferred past parse via afterParse so a sem-source snapshot never sees runtime writes).

attributes.name: type
attributes.description: one of `definition` | `extension`. Selects the banner mark (`⌜NPL@…⌝` vs `⌜extend:NPL@…⌝`) and mirrors the resolved kind to `data-type`. Any other value falls back to `definition`.

attributes.name: extend-target
attributes.description: optional; the vocabulary an extension extends, authored on `type="extension"` declarations. Rendered by `.npl-declaration-target` beside the mark whenever authored and mirrored to `data-extend-target` (absent when unauthored).

tags.name: npl-directive
tags.summary: Marks a short instruction inside a sentence, so it stands out from the prose.
tags.description: You write the instruction, and optionally a longer note, inside this element. The page shows it as a small chip the reader can spot while scanning.

attributes.name: glyph
attributes.description: required; the emoji or symbol leading the chip. Rendered by `.npl-directive-glyph` (dropped, gracefully, when absent) and mirrored to `data-glyph` when non-empty.

attributes.name: kind
attributes.description: one of `directive` | `prefix`. A `prefix` chip renders the `➤` arrow between glyph and instruction, the prefix form's source grammar. Mirrored to `data-kind` (resolved value).

attributes.name: qualifier
attributes.description: optional; a trailing label beside the instruction, rendered by `.npl-directive-qualifier` and mirrored to `data-qualifier` when non-empty.

tags.name: npl-example
tags.summary: A sample element that shows how npl-* elements are built.
tags.description: It exists to demonstrate the pattern, not to be used in real documents. Real elements replace it.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Displayed by `.npl-example-label` and mirrored to `data-label` (dual-form contract: `data-label` wins when both spellings are present, so the mirror writes the resolved value and never clobbers an authored `data-label`; deferred past parse via afterParse so a sem-source snapshot never sees runtime writes).

tags.name: npl-flag
tags.summary: One setting a reader can switch, shown as a labelled row.
tags.description: You give it a name and a value. The reader can click the row to apply the setting. If the name implies a number range, values outside it are flagged.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: required, no default. Flag identifier; its wording implies the numeric range checked on `value` (below).

attributes.name: value
attributes.description: no default. Rendered verbatim; validated only when the name implies a numeric range (case-insensitive substring of the name): `freq` checks [0.0, 1.0] (frequency flags), `factor` checks [-10, 10] (hormone factors), `threshold` must be numeric and unbounded. Any other name (pump switches, meta, …) is free-form — never validated. An out-of-range or non-numeric value is NOT an error: the flag renders with the `npl-flag-invalid` warning class on its value span.

tags.name: npl-flags
tags.summary: A group of settings shown as clickable rows.
tags.description: It wraps one or more npl-flag elements. You can add a short note above the rows to explain what they do.

attributes.name: preset
attributes.description: optional, no default (omit it entirely for no badge). One of `minimal`, `full`, `production`, `creative`, `tireless` (the NPL flag source spells these `preset:<name>`; the attribute accepts the bare word or the prefixed spelling, normalized for display). An unknown preset is NOT an error: it warns through the author-facing channel and renders with the invalid-preset warning class (see Rendered form).

tags.name: npl-hormones
tags.summary: Shows seven drive levels — like momentum, tension, and curiosity — as bars.
tags.description: Each drive has a level from 0 to 100, drawn as a bar with an arrow showing whether it rose or fell. Notes explain what a bar means when it passes a set limit.

attributes.name: variant
attributes.description: `panel` renders one row per `h` plus the `state` and `triggered` lines; `bars` renders only the rows (the compact form); `alert` renders only the `alert` elements. Any other value falls back to `panel`.

attributes.name: state
attributes.description: child element — compound state description, rendered in the `panel` variant as the state line.

attributes.name: triggered
attributes.description: child element — threshold behaviors activated, or `none`. A row is highlighted (`data-fired`) when this block names the hormone: by symbol (word match, so `RST` does not hit "first"), by name, or by its `trigger` text; `none` highlights nothing.

attributes.name: alert
attributes.description: child elements — `hormone`, `value`, `threshold`, `behavior` attributes, body text as content. Rendered only by the `alert` variant.

tags.name: npl-intent
tags.summary: Shows what a piece of work is meant to achieve: the goal, the scope, and the expected outcomes.
tags.description: You write the goal, what is in and out of scope, the outcomes, and any assumptions. The element lays them out in a clear grid so a reader can check the plan at a glance.

tags.name: npl-mindread
tags.summary: Shows what one party thinks another party believes or feels.
tags.description: You write the subject, the signals (tone, patterns, things left unsaid), and the reading drawn from them. The result is clearly labelled as a guess, not a fact.

attributes.name: confidence
attributes.description: optional, a theory-of-mind reading is a guess until corrected; authored `0..1`. Out-of-range values are **clamped** into `[0,1]` (a non-numeric authoring clamps to `0`), and the host is **marked**: `data-confidence` carries the clamped value, `data-confidence-out-of-range` the verbatim authored value, and the meter gains a `npl-mindread-confidence-out` note.

tags.name: npl-mode
tags.summary: Lists the thinking styles an agent uses, one chip per style.
tags.description: You write each mode as a child element. The main mode is marked so the reader knows which lens leads. This element only shows information; it changes nothing.

attributes.name: primary
attributes.description: Resolved in either authoring spelling (`data-primary` wins, conventions §2). Declares this the primary lens; marks the rendered chips (`npl-mode-chip-primary`) and mirrors to `data-primary` after parse — an authored `data-primary` is never clobbered by the default.

tags.name: npl-mood
tags.summary: Shows a mood with an emoji, plus an optional note on its tone.
tags.description: You write the mood in the mood attribute. Extra children can carry the tone, the context, and how the agent will approach work in this mood.

attributes.name: mood
attributes.description: required. One emoji followed by an optional qualifier string, whitespace-separated (`"🙂 wistful"`); a lone emoji is valid. Displayed by `.npl-mood-chip` and mirrored to `data-mood` (dual-form contract; the mirror is deferred past parse via afterParse so a sem-source snapshot never sees runtime writes).

tags.name: npl-poa
tags.summary: Shows a plan as a decision tree, plus the reasons each path was weighed.
tags.description: You write the tree, the reasoning with weights, and the option that was picked. The element shows all three parts; it never draws the tree for you.

attributes.name: direction
attributes.description: One of `lr` | `td`; declares the intended flow and mirrors to `data-direction` (dual-form contract, `data-` wins, mirror deferred past parse via afterParse). The fence's own `graph LR`/`graph TD` line remains the renderer's source of truth — authored source is never rewritten. Anything other than `lr`/`td` falls back to `lr` with an author-facing warning.

tags.name: npl-ref
tags.summary: Looks back at a finished turn: what went well, what to improve, and how it was checked.
tags.description: You write the assessment, the improvements, the validation, and any eval notes. The element lays them out as a review card after the work.

attributes.name: variant
attributes.description: one of `full`, `compact`, optional — `full` renders each section as a labelled block; `compact` renders one emoji line per section. Any other value resolves to `full`, and the resolved variant mirrors to `data-variant` (dual-form contract; the mirror is deferred past parse via afterParse, like sem-note, so a sem-source snapshot never sees runtime writes). The variant is read at upgrade; it is display-only and not switched after wiring.

tags.name: npl-rubric
tags.summary: A scoring table: each row is a criterion with a weight and a score, plus a total.
tags.description: You write the criteria, their weights, and their scores. The total is shown as given, or worked out from the weights. Wrong or missing numbers are flagged, not hidden.

attributes.name: title
attributes.description: (empty). Rendered as the table caption and mirrored to `data-title` (dual-form contract; the mirror is deferred past parse via afterParse so a sem-source snapshot never sees runtime writes).

attributes.name: npl-overall-score
attributes.description: (optional, one) — `value`: number — default: the element's trimmed text (`value` wins when both are present). States the overall score; when absent or non-numeric the component computes the weighted average — sum(weight · score) ÷ sum(weight) over the criteria with a numeric weight AND score (all-zero weights ⇒ no figure).

tags.name: npl-section
tags.summary: A labelled section for any NPL prompt block.
tags.description: Known section types get a matching header; unknown types get a warning style so a typo is easy to spot. The content stays plain text, so search and copy still work.

attributes.name: type
attributes.description: required. One of the known section types: `alg`, `alg-pseudo`, `diagram`, `example`, `format`, `logic`, `note`, `syntax`, `template`.

tags.name: npl-thought
tags.summary: A thought bubble: short related ideas grouped under one type.
tags.description: Each child is one thought with a type attribute, such as a question or a risk. The element shows them as a tidy list of bubbles.

attributes.name: type
attributes.description: optional; One of the eleven NPL thought-block types (case-insensitive): `observation`, `tangent`, `question`, `relation`, `concern`, `affirmation`, `reflection`, `opportunity`, `aversion`, `interest`, `eval`.

tags.name: npl-vos
tags.summary: Shows a persona's inner state: id, ego, superego, and mood, before a reply.
tags.description: You write each part of the state. The element shows them as labelled parts of one bracket. An optional collective part covers group personas.

attributes.name: phase
attributes.description: One of `entry`, `exit`; rendered as the bracket label and mirrored to data-phase (dual-form contract; the mirror is deferred past parse via afterParse so a sem-source snapshot never sees runtime writes).

tags.name: highlight
tags.summary: Prose with parts the reader can hide to test their recall.
tags.description: You wrap the words to remember in a highlight child, or use [[double brackets]] as shorthand. Hiding them turns the passage into a self-test; showing them again reveals the answers.

tags.name: sem-api-call
tags.summary: Documents one API call's contract: method, endpoint, status and its parameters, as a card.
tags.description: The definition card for an endpoint. You write the operation name, HTTP method and path, then one sem-api-param child per parameter or response field; the page shows a table and machines read the same fields back.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: (on `sem-api-call`): required, string — the operation's display name.

attributes.name: method
attributes.description: (optional): string token — HTTP method, rendered uppercased, extraction records the authored spelling uppercased.

attributes.name: status
attributes.description: (optional): string — the documented response status ("200", "2xx", "201 Created" …).

tags.name: sem-api-param
tags.summary: One parameter row inside a sem-api-call: name, where it lives, type and description.
tags.description: The child of sem-api-call. The in attribute says where the parameter lives (query, body, header, or response for a returned field); required marks the ones the caller must send.

tags.name: sem-audiences
tags.summary: Names the reader groups a document knows about, so each reader sees the parts meant for them.
tags.description: You list each group here, then mark sections with an audience attribute. The reader picks their group and the page hides the rest. Nothing is deleted — machines still read the whole document.

attributes.name: id
attributes.description: (required, document-unique): the profile token that `audience` specs and the hash parameter refer to. It is an ordinary element id, so it shares the document's id space.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: (optional): human label; the id renders when absent.

attributes.name: implies
attributes.description: (optional, comma list): profiles this one satisfies as well. `operator implies reader` means an operator sees reader content. Closure is transitive; a cycle is an authoring error, warned once and broken.

tags.name: sem-browser
tags.summary: Draws a browser-style window around a live SemText document.
tags.description: It gives the document an address bar and a window frame, while everything inside stays real, working SemText. Use it when a page demonstrates a document rather than being one.

attributes.name: src
attributes.description: (optional): VFS path or URL of the SemText document to render. With no `src`, the element's authored children are the viewport content.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: (optional): tab-label override. Priority: `label`, then the document's `<title>`, then the `src` basename, then `untitled`.

attributes.name: resolve
attributes.description: (property only, not an attribute): a host-injected `(path) => string | null | Promise<string | null>` consulted for scheme-less paths (`demo/deck.sem.html`, not `/…` or `https://…`) before any fetch. Returning a string adopts it; returning null errors without fetching.

tags.name: sem-changelog
tags.summary: A changelog: dated entries describing what changed.
tags.description: You wrap the collection in sem-changelogs and write one entry per change inside, each with its date and a name. It stays ordinary readable text with JavaScript off.

tags.name: sem-changelogs
tags.summary: The collection wrapper for changelog entries.
tags.description: You set the kind — added, changed, fixed, removed — on each entry, and the chrome labels the collection. The entries themselves are the record; nothing is invented.

attributes.name: date
attributes.description: per entry; the authored stamp (YYYY-MM-DD), drawn into the entry heading chrome.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: `title`: per the global/standard attribute catalog — entry heading qualifiers, drawn into the entry chrome.

tags.name: sem-chronology
tags.summary: A timeline: dated events shown in the order they happened.
tags.description: Each child is one event with a when date, an optional end date, and an optional status. You write the events in order; the element never sorts them. It can show the events as a timeline rail or as a plain list.

attributes.name: when
attributes.description: (recommended): the event's date or period start, as the author wants a machine to see it (ISO-8601 preferred, free text allowed).

attributes.name: status
attributes.description: (optional): `done | current | todo | blocked` — same vocabulary as `sem-step`. Absent means unannotated, **not** `todo`: an event is a record of something that happened, not a task.

tags.name: sem-code
tags.summary: A code listing with a file name, a language, and marked lines.
tags.description: The code is shown exactly as written — spacing included. You can mark the lines that matter, and the reader gets copy controls a plain code block cannot offer.

attributes.name: lang
attributes.description: (optional): language token, rendered as a badge.

attributes.name: mark
attributes.description: (optional): emphasised lines, 1-based, comma list of numbers and `a-b` ranges (`2,4-5`). Out-of-range entries are ignored.

attributes.name: controls
attributes.description: (optional): comma flags from `copy`, `wrap`; Unknown flags are ignored.

tags.name: sem-data-join
tags.summary: Combines two named data sets on one shared column, like a database join.
tags.description: You name the two sources and the key column. The joined result becomes a new data set that queries can use. Nothing shows on the page by itself — it only feeds queries.

attributes.name: data-name
attributes.description: (alias `name`): required — bucket key of the join result; colliding with a source name is an authoring error.

attributes.name: data-left
attributes.description: (alias `left`): required — the left-hand bucket to join, by `data-name` reference.

attributes.name: data-right
attributes.description: (alias `right`): required — the other bucket to join, by `data-name` reference.

attributes.name: data-on
attributes.description: (alias `on`): required — the named key column; must exist (case-insensitive) in both buckets.

tags.name: sem-data-query
tags.summary: A question asked of a data set, written in a small, safe SQL-like language.
tags.description: You write one query: pick columns, filter, sort, and limit. Joins are declared separately, and nothing can change the data. Readers see the results, and the query text stays visible.

tags.name: sem-data-source
tags.summary: One named set of data inside a data visualizer.
tags.description: You either write the data inside the element or point at a file with source. Doing both is an error the element reports clearly. With JavaScript off, the data still reads as text.

attributes.name: data-name
attributes.description: free text — human label rendered as the table `caption`, and the bucket key every query, join and cross-source view reference resolves (exact, then case-insensitive, then normalized: lowercase, non-alphanumeric runs collapsed to `-`, edge `-` trimmed).

attributes.name: data-format
attributes.description: (optional): one of `table`, `csv`, `yaml`, `json`, `sql` — payload syntax of the body or of the fetched resource; Unknown format is a clear inline error, never a silent blank.

attributes.name: data-type
attributes.description: (optional): one of `rows`, `yaml-schema` — structure declaration; (absent ⇒ the tier infers). rows ⇒ simple row/column definition via the per-column declaration attribute; yaml-schema ⇒ the payload is an OpenAPI-style YAML document whose nested objects flatten to dotted column paths.

attributes.name: data-columns
attributes.description: (optional): string — with `data-type="rows"`, the per-column declaration, a comma list of `name[:type][?]` (`?` = nullable; types `string`, `number`, `integer`, `boolean`, `date`, `null`). Declared types override inference per column; inference fills any column the declaration omits.

attributes.name: source
attributes.description: (optional): string — URL of a relative/same-origin file or an absolute `http(s)` file/API endpoint; inline payload and `source` are mutually exclusive. `file://` is refused when the document itself is `file://`.

attributes.name: data-views
attributes.description: (optional): named views as `name=colspec; name=colspec` — `colspec` is `*` or a comma list of column names, matched case-insensitively; malformed segments are skipped (a typo hides a view, it never breaks the document).

attributes.name: data-view
attributes.description: (optional): view name — the default view. Resolution: `data-view` name ⇒ first declared view ⇒ implicit `all=*`.

attributes.name: data-header
attributes.description: (optional): one of `true`, `false`; csv only: `false` ⇒ the first row is data and headers synthesize `col-<n>`.

attributes.name: data-path
attributes.description: (optional): string — `json`/API only: dot/bracket path into a nested response (`data.items`, `rows[2].entries`) that flattens to the row array.

attributes.name: data-cache
attributes.description: (optional): one of `no`; `no` ⇒ skip the in-memory fetch cache (one fetch per URL per page load by default).

tags.name: sem-data-visualizer
tags.summary: The container that holds data sets, joins, and queries, and shows the results.
tags.description: You put one or more sem-data-source children inside, plus any joins and queries. The container owns the shared state: which data set and query are active. With JavaScript off it shows the data as plain tables.

attributes.name: id
attributes.description: optional — names the container for the modal deep link (`#dv=<visualizer-id>`). The copy-link chrome prefers the container's id; with none it falls back to the container's sole named source (`#bucket=<name>`), and a container with neither mints no copy-link button.

tags.name: sem-detail
tags.summary: One passage of prose with parts that can be hidden for self-testing.
tags.description: This is the child of sem-details. Wrap the words to recall in a highlight, or use [[double brackets]]. Hiding them turns the passage into a memory exercise.

tags.name: sem-details
tags.summary: A group of passages whose key words can be hidden for recall practice.
tags.description: Each sem-detail child is one passage. Readers hide or show the highlighted words to test themselves. This is a study aid — not a reveal box and not a tab set.

attributes.name: view-as
attributes.description: `plain` (default) | `quiz`. Display-only sugar — the prose is identical; quiz view additionally occludes highlights.

attributes.name: id
attributes.description: on the container; `kind`, `tags` global. Facts may also carry `<highlight>` prompts (schema sem-facts), but occlusion wiring for prose lives here.

tags.name: sem-eval
tags.summary: An evaluation spec: the inputs, expected outputs and criteria in one container.
tags.description: You author the cases as sections or prose inside; the container adds the chrome and label. It states what a good answer looks like — it does not run anything.

attributes.name: kind
attributes.description: optional qualifier drawn into the label chrome (display-only sugar).

attributes.name: status
attributes.description: one of `draft`, `approved`, `implemented` — lifecycle token, drawn as a status chip (display-only).

tags.name: sem-event
tags.summary: One dated event on a timeline.
tags.description: You give it a when date, an optional until end date, and an optional status such as planned or done. Its place in the page is its place in time — the element does not sort events.

tags.name: sem-fact
tags.summary: One fact: a statement, its conclusion, and optionally what would be wrong to believe.
tags.description: You write the statement, the conclusion drawn from it, and any incorrect-statement to warn against. The id is the token other text cites. It reads as plain sentences with JavaScript off.

tags.name: sem-facts
tags.summary: A group of facts the reader can flip through as cards, a quiz, or plain prose.
tags.description: You wrap sem-fact children in it and pick a view with view-as. The view only changes how the facts are shown — the facts themselves stay the same, and machines always read all of them.

attributes.name: view-as
attributes.description: `list` (default) | `flashcards` | `quiz`. Canonical attribute; display-only sugar — machines extract the same pairs regardless of view.

attributes.name: id
attributes.description: on the container and on facts: required for citation (`#auth-facts/f-rotate`); `kind`, `tags` global.

tags.name: sem-faq
tags.summary: One FAQ entry: the asked question and its authored answer.
tags.description: The question child is the question; everything you write in the answer child is the answer. Machines extract both verbatim; the browser can show them as a Q and A pair.

tags.name: sem-faqs
tags.summary: A collection of FAQ entries.
tags.description: You wrap sem-faq children in it. The view only changes how the questions and answers are shown — the words stay the same.

attributes.name: kind
attributes.description: collection qualifier drawn into the label chrome (display-only sugar).

tags.name: sem-file-tree
tags.summary: A file listing written as an indented tree inside a pre block.
tags.description: You type the tree with box-drawing characters or plain indentation; with JavaScript on the same engine as sem-site-tree turns it into a browsable listing, and with JavaScript off the pre is the record.

tags.name: sem-guard-rail
tags.summary: One guard rail: a rule the reader should not cross.
tags.description: You give it a severity and a scope, and write the rule as the content. It renders as a labelled, warning-level item in the guard-rails list.

tags.name: sem-guard-rails
tags.summary: A collection of guard rails.
tags.description: You wrap sem-guard-rail children in it. The collection sorts nothing and invents nothing — the rails you wrote, in the order you wrote them.

attributes.name: kind
attributes.description: collection qualifier drawn into the label chrome (display-only sugar).

attributes.name: severity
attributes.description: (per entry): one of `info` (default), `warn`, `block` — selects the rail color; display-only sugar, extraction is identical under every severity.

attributes.name: scope
attributes.description: (per entry): `string` — free token naming where the rule applies; drawn into the entry's label chrome.

tags.name: sem-howto
tags.summary: A how-to guide container: a named guide with free contents.
tags.description: The name child is the title; everything else inside is the guide. The container adds the chrome and label — you write the steps with the elements you already have.

tags.name: sem-kb
tags.summary: A knowledge-base article: the content you write inside is the article.
tags.description: There is no special structure to learn — headings, prose and the other elements all work as usual. The container frames the article with a labelled panel.

attributes.name: kind
attributes.description: optional topical qualifier, drawn into the label chrome (display-only sugar; extraction is identical either way).

tags.name: sem-md
tags.summary: A block written in Markdown that the browser turns into HTML.
tags.description: You write tables, lists, and other Markdown inside the element. Readers see a formatted table or list; machines get the Markdown back unchanged. Made for content that is easier to write as Markdown than as HTML.

attributes.name: view-as
attributes.description: (optional): `rendered` (default) or `raw` — the initial mode. **Mutable presentation**: the toggle rewrites `data-view-as` at runtime (the authored bare attribute is left alone) and extraction ignores it (spec/extraction.md §5c).

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: (optional): a short caption rendered in the chrome.

attributes.name: controls
attributes.description: (optional): comma flags from `toggle`, `copy`; default both, also when the attribute is present but empty. Unknown flags are ignored.

tags.name: sem-mockup
tags.summary: A UI mockup container holding text or HTML.
tags.description: You pick the mode — text or html — and put the mockup inside. It renders as a framed specimen; nothing inside it is interactive.

attributes.name: mode
attributes.description: one of `text` (default), `html` — presentation selector; display-only sugar.

attributes.name: kind
attributes.description: optional qualifier drawn into the label chrome.

tags.name: sem-note
tags.summary: A callout: a short piece of prose set beside the main text.
tags.description: Pick a variant — info, warning, tip, or danger — for the colour and label. The collapsed attribute hides the body behind a short teaser. It stays ordinary readable text with JavaScript off.

attributes.name: collapsed
attributes.description: boolean attr — the body is hidden behind a ten-word teaser (`.sem-note-summary`) that expands on click.

attributes.name: view-as
attributes.description: presentation only. On wide viewports the note floats right beside the prose that follows it (width `--sem-margin-width`, default 14rem), inside the container; a document whose column has a gutter pushes it out with `--sem-margin-offset`. On narrow viewports and in print it reads inline as an ordinary callout. CSS-only — no handler, no chrome, no record change.

tags.name: sem-philosophy
tags.summary: A principles container: the beliefs or rules a project runs on.
tags.description: You write the principles inside as prose or lists. The container gives them a labelled home so machines can find the project's stated principles.

attributes.name: kind
attributes.description: optional qualifier drawn into the label chrome (display-only sugar).

tags.name: sem-plan
tags.summary: A plan container: the reasoning and the steps of a solution.
tags.description: You write the plan inside as sections or prose, with an optional status. The container keeps the reasoning with the work it produced.

attributes.name: kind
attributes.description: optional qualifier drawn into the label chrome (display-only sugar).

attributes.name: status
attributes.description: per the global catalog (`done`, `current`, `todo`, `blocked`, `pass`, `fail`) — drawn as a status chip (display-only).

tags.name: sem-procedure
tags.summary: An ordered list of steps, each marked with where it stands.
tags.description: You write one sem-step per step, in the order they happen. Each step carries a status: done, current, todo, or blocked. There are no step numbers to maintain — position is the number.

tags.name: sem-profile
tags.summary: Names one reader group inside a sem-audiences block.
tags.description: You give it an id and a short label. Sections tagged with this id show or hide as the reader switches groups.

tags.name: sem-progress
tags.summary: A progress bar for one number between 0 and 1.
tags.description: You give it a value and an optional label. The page draws a bar with the percentage. Values outside the range are clamped for display, and the raw value still reads as text without JavaScript.

attributes.name: value
attributes.description: required, canonical unit 0..1. Out-of-range values clamp for rendering; the raw attr stays untouched (machine readers see the author's value, the render shows the clamp).

attributes.name: status
attributes.description: optional completion state — pairs with value 1 and renders the full/accent state (same catalog as `sem-step`).

tags.name: sem-properties
tags.summary: A list of key–value pairs, shown as a tidy definition grid.
tags.description: You write one sem-property per pair. The grid renders with plain CSS, so it works with JavaScript off. Machines read the same pairs back.

attributes.name: key
attributes.description: (on each `sem-property`): required, free text (the term). The property text is the value.

attributes.name: view-as
attributes.description: (optional; R/W1): the block is a glossary. Each property should carry an `id`; prose elsewhere links a term with a plain anchor (`JWT`), optionally wrapping it in `` at its defining use.

tags.name: sem-property
tags.summary: One key–value pair in a properties grid.
tags.description: The key attribute is the term; the text inside is its meaning. Add role=definition when the value defines the key.

tags.name: sem-reader
tags.summary: Reading tools for a long document: an outline, a progress bar, and controls for text size and theme.
tags.description: It is page furniture, not content — a document without it loses nothing a machine would read. Readers get focus mode, type size, colour scheme, print, and audience controls in one place.

attributes.name: controls
attributes.description: optional. Comma flags, in any order, one of `outline`, `progress`, `focus`, `type`, `color`, `print`, `audience` — unknown flags, including the theme flag reserved for R/W3, are ignored. Controls render in the **canonical order** above, not in attribute order.

attributes.name: outline-depth
attributes.description: optional. Deepest heading level in the generated outline, `2`–`6`; The outline always starts at `h2` — `h1` is the document title.

tags.name: sem-reference
tags.summary: One numbered entry in a reference list.
tags.description: You give it an id, a link, and a note. In the text, cite it with a plain link to the id. The element carries the fields a plain list item cannot.

tags.name: sem-references
tags.summary: A numbered list of sources the document cites.
tags.description: You wrap one sem-reference per source. Numbers come from position. With JavaScript off the list still reads as an ordinary numbered list.

attributes.name: kind
attributes.description: `footnotes` | `bibliography` (free token; these two get distinct styling). Optional.

attributes.name: id
attributes.description: (required; on each `sem-reference`): the citation target — the global `id`.

attributes.name: href
attributes.description: (optional; on each `sem-reference`): external location (`data-href` in the class form).

tags.name: sem-requirement
tags.summary: A requirement statement with a status and priority.
tags.description: You write the requirement as the content and set kind, status and priority as attributes. Machines read it as one requirement record; readers see a labelled statement.

attributes.name: kind
attributes.description: one of `functional`, `non-functional`, `constraint` — the requirement class, drawn into the label chrome.

attributes.name: status
attributes.description: one of `draft`, `approved`, `implemented` — lifecycle token, drawn as a status chip (display-only).

attributes.name: priority
attributes.description: free token (e.g. `high`); drawn into the status chip when present.

tags.name: sem-reveal
tags.summary: A question the reader clicks to reveal the answer.
tags.description: You write the question as the summary and the answer as the body. It is a plain details box, so it works with JavaScript off. Use it for explanation — a sem-fact is for claims.

attributes.name: summary
attributes.description: optional label for the closed state. Default: the leading body text (max 60 chars, cut at the last word boundary, trailing punctuation dropped) acts as summary when absent.

attributes.name: open
attributes.description: boolean attr — starts **revealed** (no control; the body is live immediately; the host carries `data-revealed`).

attributes.name: collapsed
attributes.description: boolean attr — accepted, no-op. Hidden is the default.

tags.name: sem-rubric
tags.summary: A scoring rubric container: criteria against levels.
tags.description: You author the grid inside as a plain table or row prose — the container does not force a shape. Set max-score and the chrome shows the scale.

attributes.name: max-score
attributes.description: the scale ceiling (minimum 0); drawn into the label chrome as a chip when present.

tags.name: sem-runbook
tags.summary: An operational runbook: preconditions, procedure and references in one container.
tags.description: You author the parts inside with the elements you already use; the container adds the chrome and a label. It reads as a document and extracts as one runbook record.

attributes.name: kind
attributes.description: optional qualifier drawn into the label chrome (display-only sugar).

attributes.name: audience
attributes.description: `any` — per the global catalog (`sem-audiences`); the runbook itself does no audience gating, the document profiles do.

tags.name: sem-site-tree
tags.summary: A site or file tree written as nested node elements.
tags.description: You nest bare node children with a path and optional label and kind. The same engine that reads sem-file-tree renders it, so both notations share one model.

tags.name: sem-source
tags.summary: Lets the reader flip between a section as it renders and the markup behind it.
tags.description: You put ordinary SemText inside. The reader sees the rendered result, then the exact source that produced it. Made for documents that teach the vocabulary.

attributes.name: view-as
attributes.description: `html` (default) | `source`. The initial mode. Mutable presentation: the toggle rewrites `data-view-as` at runtime (the authored bare attribute is left alone), and extraction ignores it (spec/extraction.md §5c).

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: (optional): a short caption rendered in the chrome.

tags.name: sem-step
tags.summary: One step in a procedure.
tags.description: You write the instruction as the text and set status to done, current, todo, or blocked. Its place in the page is its order in the procedure.

tags.name: sem-summary
tags.summary: A summary container: the short version of what follows.
tags.description: Everything you put inside is the record. The container labels it as a summary so skimmers and machines both know what it is.

attributes.name: kind
attributes.description: optional qualifier drawn into the label chrome (display-only sugar).

tags.name: sem-table
tags.summary: A table the reader can sort and filter — the table you write is the data.
tags.description: You write a normal HTML table. Sorting and filtering only change what the reader sees; the markup stays the contract, so machines always read the same rows you wrote.

attributes.name: data-value
attributes.description: (optional, on `<td>`): the sort key for that cell when the visible text is not the key (`15 min` vs `900`). Two numeric keys compare numerically; anything else compares as text, locale-aware.

attributes.name: controls
attributes.description: (optional): one of the comma flags `sort`, `filter`; Unknown flags are ignored.

attributes.name: sticky
attributes.description: (boolean, optional): the header row sticks to the top of the scroll container. Opting in also caps the element at `max-height: 24rem` so a long table scrolls inside itself — the stick needs an internal scroll container to engage, and without it a page-level table never gains one and the header would scroll away like any other row. CSS only — works with scripts off.

tags.name: sem-tag-attr
tags.summary: One attribute row inside a sem-tag-def: name, type, required flag, default and description.
tags.description: The child of sem-tag-def. You write the attribute's name and type, add the required flag when it must be present, and the description text is what readers see in that row.

tags.name: sem-tag-def
tags.summary: Documents one tag's contract: its attributes, types, defaults and child tags, as a card.
tags.description: The definition card for a markup tag. You write the tag name and one sem-tag-attr child per attribute; the page shows a tidy table and machines read the same fields back. The reference pages use it, so the vocabulary documents itself.

attributes.name: tag
attributes.description: (on `sem-tag-def`): required, string — the documented tag's name (backtick-free, strict tag shape).

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: (optional): string — human display name ("Note") when it differs from the tag name.

attributes.name: group
attributes.description: (optional): free token — grouping label for reference indexes (`annotation`, `layout`, `data` …).

attributes.name: children
attributes.description: (optional): comma/space token list — the documented tag's child tags.

tags.name: sem-threat-model
tags.summary: A threat-model container: assets, threats and mitigations.
tags.description: You author them inside as sections or list prose; the container adds the chrome, label and scope. It frames the analysis — it does not check it.

attributes.name: kind
attributes.description: optional methodology qualifier drawn into the label chrome (display-only sugar).

attributes.name: scope
attributes.description: free token naming the modelled boundary; drawn into the label chrome when present.

tags.name: sem-tldr
tags.summary: A summary block the reader can skim or skip.
tags.description: Whatever you put inside is the whole record — the element adds nothing and hides nothing. It renders as a set-apart block so the gist is visible at a glance.

tags.name: sem-tsg
tags.summary: One troubleshooting entry: a symptom and its fix.
tags.description: You write the problem and the resolution inside; the entry stays ordinary readable text with JavaScript off.

tags.name: sem-tsgs
tags.summary: A collection of troubleshooting entries.
tags.description: You wrap sem-tsg children in it. The collection is the record — the entries you wrote, in the order you wrote them.

attributes.name: kind
attributes.description: collection qualifier drawn into the label chrome (display-only sugar).

tags.name: sem-view
tags.summary: One named perspective inside a sem-views tab set.
tags.description: The name attribute labels the tab; the content inside is that view of the subject. With JavaScript off every view shows, each under its name.

tags.name: sem-views
tags.summary: Shows one subject several ways, with a tab bar to switch.
tags.description: You wrap sem-view children and name each one. Readers switch by click, keyboard, or link. The content is never moved or rewritten — only which view shows changes.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: required, unique within the container, human label.

attributes.name: active
attributes.description: boolean marker on the initially-visible view; **if no view carries it, the first view is active**. The shown view is tracked at runtime in `data-active` (the component mirrors an authored `active` there, then moves it on every switch); the authored attribute is never rewritten.

attributes.name: id
attributes.description: required **for enhancement, not only for deep links** — the handler selects `.sem-views[id]`, so a container without an id never upgrades and stays stacked (the JS-off form) even with script running. Also the deep-link head (`#deploy/argocd`); `kind`, `tags` global.

tags.name: sem-workflow
tags.summary: An ordered workflow whose steps carry verification.
tags.description: You write one sem-step per step, like a procedure, plus a duration for the whole run. Each step can carry a gate and check, and an if-no that says what to do when the check fails.

tags.name: semext-annotate
tags.summary: Visitor comment threads embedded in the page, backed by the annotate service.
tags.description: The embed renders the cached threads snapshot; it is the one embed of the family with a live anonymous read. Visitors pin comments on the page and the embed shows them in place.

attributes.name: site
attributes.description: the annotate site slug; query parameter on the live read; optional for a snapshot-only embed.

attributes.name: page
attributes.description: the page path the threads belong to; query parameter on the live read (the snapshot's `page` field should match); optional for a snapshot-only embed.

attributes.name: endpoint
attributes.description: the annotate API **base** (e.g. `https://annotate-srv.therobotlives.com/api/v1`); the element resolves the threads collection `<endpoint>/threads?site=<site>&page=<page>` — the path + query shape THIS contract defines, the annotate service owns the canonical shape. Optional in snapshot mode.

tags.name: semext-docptr
tags.summary: A doc-pointer card rendered from a cached snapshot.
tags.description: The snapshot mirrors the pointer registry so a page can cite a source location durably — the card survives line drift until a CLI refresh re-snapshots it.

attributes.name: marker
attributes.description: full marker string (e.g. `〚🔧:uuid〛`); selects the entry whose marker matches.

attributes.name: uuid
attributes.description: the pointer's full UUID; the strongest selector.

attributes.name: token
attributes.description: the pointer's 4-glyph token; selects by token match against the entry's marker.

attributes.name: file
attributes.description: narrows selection to entries whose `file_path` equals this path (filter, applied after the identifier selectors).

tags.name: semext-media-prompt
tags.summary: An authored media-generation prompt with an output cache region.
tags.description: The record is the prompt you write; the output region beside it is filled by the refresh CLI, not the element. The element never fetches and never generates — it only reports the region's state.

attributes.name: model
attributes.description: the generation model slug (rendered in the params line; echoed verbatim).

attributes.name: aspect
attributes.description: the aspect token (rendered in the params line).

attributes.name: assets-dir
attributes.description: the directory the refresh CLI writes relative asset paths into (rendered in the params line).

tags.name: semext-sig-logs
tags.summary: A SigNoz log-line snapshot with a link to open the query.
tags.description: The log lines you author are the record; the chrome builds an Open in SigNoz anchor from the query, range and env you set. The snapshot is refreshed by the CLI, never fetched at read time.

attributes.name: query
attributes.description: the SigNoz query expression (deep-link parameter; echoed verbatim, never parsed).

tags.name: semext-sig-metrics
tags.summary: A SigNoz metrics snapshot with a link to open the query.
tags.description: The metrics table you author is the record; the chrome adds the deep link from your query parameters. Nothing is fetched when the page is read.

attributes.name: query
attributes.description: the SigNoz query expression (deep-link parameter; echoed verbatim, never parsed).

tags.name: semext-sig-synthetic-monitor
tags.summary: A SigNoz synthetic-monitor definition card with a deep link.
tags.description: You author the monitor's expected definition; the card mirrors it and links to SigNoz. Running monitors is a service surface this element deliberately does not touch.

attributes.name: monitor
attributes.description: the monitor's identity (deep-link parameter; echoed verbatim, never parsed).

tags.name: semext-sig-traces
tags.summary: A SigNoz trace-list snapshot with a link to open the query.
tags.description: The trace list you author is the record; the chrome adds the Open in SigNoz anchor. The embed is cached and link-only — no client queries.

attributes.name: query
attributes.description: the SigNoz query expression (deep-link parameter; echoed verbatim, never parsed).

tags.name: semext-styleguide-theme
tags.summary: One theme's token cards rendered from a cached snapshot.
tags.description: The card shows the theme name, key color swatches and a type sample, plus a link to preview the theme CSS at the src you set. Refresh is the CLI lane.

attributes.name: theme
attributes.description: the theme slug this card presents; matches the snapshot's theme slug when one is authored.

attributes.name: src
attributes.description: the theme CSS URL for the preview link; MUST pass the shared source policy (src/data/load.ts: http(s) only, rendered as an href — never fetched by this element). Omitting it omits the link.

tags.name: semext-styleguide-themes
tags.summary: The collection wrapper for theme token cards.
tags.description: It renders a summary line over its semext-styleguide-theme children. The snapshots are refreshed by the CLI, not at read time.

tags.name: sem-enhanced-document
tags.summary: The required root wrapper around a SemText document.
tags.description: You wrap the whole document in it once. Inside, plain HTML and sem-* elements mix freely. Extraction reads everything inside the wrapper; the browser treats it as an ordinary container.

tags.name: agent
tags.summary: Describes one AI agent inside the document: its name, a short bio, and its instructions.
tags.description: You write name, bio, and instructions as plain children. The browser ignores this element; extraction turns it into one agent record. Use it when the document is addressed to or about an agent.

tags.name: statement
tags.summary: The claim side of a fact — what is asserted.
tags.description: You write the statement as the child of a sem-fact. Its pair, the conclusion, draws the takeaway. Plain text, no attributes needed.

tags.name: conclusion
tags.summary: The takeaway side of a fact — what the statement means.
tags.description: You write it inside a sem-fact, after the statement. Flashcard views show it on the answer side; extraction pairs it with the statement.

tags.name: incorrect-statement
tags.summary: A wrong version of a fact, shown so readers can spot the error.
tags.description: You write it inside a sem-fact. Quiz views can offer it as a wrong answer choice; extraction keeps it labelled as false — never as a claim.

tags.name: sem-question
tags.summary: A question with answer choices, for self-testing.
tags.description: You write the question and one or more sem-option children. It pairs with the quiz views of sem-facts. Works as plain markup with JavaScript off.

tags.name: sem-option
tags.summary: One answer choice in a question.
tags.description: The correct attribute marks the right choice. Readers pick an answer; machines read which option was correct.

buckets.label: Document & structure
buckets.description: The root wrapper, reading chrome, audience declarations and document-level metadata that frame a SemText document.

buckets.label: Prose & code
buckets.description: Content blocks beyond plain HTML — Markdown bodies, callouts, skim blocks and source listings with provenance.

buckets.label: Disclosure & views
buckets.description: The same content under different reading interactions — occluded detail, Q→A reveal, markup flip, perspective tabs.

buckets.label: Facts & recall
buckets.description: Assertable statement/conclusion pairs — the citable unit — with the quiz candidates and distractors built on them.

buckets.label: Data & tables
buckets.description: Authored tables, site/file trees, and the data-visualizer's named buckets, joins and editable queries.

buckets.label: Sequences & progress
buckets.description: Ordered, status-annotated content — timelines, procedures, verified workflows and completion meters.

buckets.label: Knowledge & documents
buckets.description: Whole-document containers for a named genre — how-tos, runbooks, KBs, FAQs, changelogs, guard-rails, plans, requirements, rubrics, evals, philosophies, summaries, threat models and mockups — each a self-describing wrapper with its own metadata and sections.

buckets.label: Definitions & citations
buckets.description: Closed key/value assertions, the numbered works the prose cites, and the self-describing vocabulary cards (tag/attribute/API definitions).
